paragraphs: Friend, here's what David teaches me in Psalm 63. He's in the Wilderness of Judah, a place with no water, and the first thing he reaches for is God. He doesn't say he's thirsty for a way out. He says, "my soul thirsts for You." (Psalm 63:1) So when life gets dry, your first move can be the same one: go to God Himself.

Now watch how David can say that. He remembers seeing God's "power and glory" in the sanctuary, and he decides God's loving devotion is "better than life." (Psalm 63:2-3) That's why he can promise to bless God "as long as I live." (Psalm 63:4) His soul is satisfied "as with the richest of foods" while the land around him is STILL dry. (Psalm 63:5) The wilderness didn't change first. His hold on God did.

And that hold goes both ways, baker. David says, "My soul clings to You; Your right hand upholds me." (Psalm 63:8) Even in the night, when his mind wanders to the people who seek his life, he keeps coming back to God, and he ends with joy in God, not fear. (Psalm 63:6, 11) I know a little about long, dark stretches, and I'm telling you, God holds on tighter than we do. So hold on to Him, and let the dry places teach you how good He is.
